data.reasoning: The package is a standard dictionary add-on for aspell. The PKGBUILD downloads a source tarball from a legitimate GNU Savannah URL with pinned MD5 and SHA256 checksums, and uses standard build/install steps. The disagreement between the models was caused solely by a transient API error (HTTP 400) in the first model when reviewing a LICENSE file, not by any actual security concern. The second model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The first model (qwen) returned 'inconclusive' because it encountered an HTTP 400 BadRequestError from the LLM API while auditing one of the LICENSE files. The second model (deepseek) successfully audited the same files and returned 'safe'. The disagreement is purely an artifact of a tool/API failure, not a difference in security assessment.
coverage_issues: Report 1 failed to audit one of the LICENSE files due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400), leading to an overall inconclusive verdict.
learnings: The audit tool should implement retry logic or graceful degradation for transient LLM API errors (like HTTP 400/500) on non-executable files (e.g., LICENSE, README). Failing the entire package audit as 'inconclusive' due to an API error on a static text file is overly brittle.
